summary: Reconciliation of three validated stage-1 proposals (vehicle_ai_and_pit_01, wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_01, wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_02) covering per-frame AI driver control, pit-stop strategy and execution, tire physics, and the AI racing-line/roster helpers. Three proposals name the same class F1CVehicle with complementary method sets (AI tick graph 0x00424E70, pit/command-queue graph 0x00424CD0, vehicle-root obj-base samples) and agreeing per-vehicle-container responsibilities, so they are merged into one canonical family; the wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_02:6 obj-base samples are kept as boundary clues and the possibility of a distinct unnamed sub-object is recorded. F1CPitMachine, F1CVehicleTireSystem, F1CAIRacingLineTracker, TirePhysicsModel and the smaller helper families keep their packet ownership and trust and are not merged on shared-offset grounds. Output: 3 engine subsystems covering all 52 required functions, 14 canonical type families, 6 state machines, 10 interfaces, 21 compatibility contracts, and a representative dependency set. Conflicts between proposals (0x0042A110 name, 0x4550/0x45E0/0x45F4/0x32C8 multi-use fields, session-phase and wear-mode literal-vs-prose gaps, tire-system identity) are recorded, not erased. No CONFIRMED/FACT promotion; trust ceiling DERIVED.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleAIPitControl
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame AI driver control and pit-stop decision logic for race vehicles: AI tick orchestration (pre-race init vs racing path), waypoint/racing-line following, steering-target computation and lane scoring, driver-status state machine, AI ability drift, and tire-compound pit-stop scheduling with retirement.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleAIAndPit
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Per-frame AI decision-making for vehicles and pit-stop strategy/timing: difficulty scaling, steering and racing-line correction, AI command queueing, pit-entry/exit forcing, fuel and tire strategy, driver-table event reporting, per-vehicle tire physics, and the fixed-tick main loop that drives them.

engine_subsystems.name: VehicleAIAndPitOperations
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Vehicle-side AI and pit operations: pit-machine state machine (pit-box alignment, pit-stop readiness, per-frame pit-stop progress with speed limiter and wheel-force ramps), racing-line/path following with target-node traversal, tire physics force computation (sign-selected lookup tables, friction-circle model, wear simulation), tire brand catalog lookup, and AI opponent roster selection.

canonical_type_families.name: F1CVehicle
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Merged per-vehicle container of the AI field block (roughly this+0x4000..0x461C), shared vehicle fields (position, velocity, heading, steering inputs), and pit/command-queue/fuel/tire sub-state; the vehicle root is reached via this+0x0 (obj base). Three proposals name the same class with complementary method sets (AI tick graph from vehicle_ai_and_pit_01:0, pit/command-queue graph from wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_01:0, vehicle-root obj-base samples from wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_02:6) and agreeing responsibilities.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Field samples from the three source proposals are retained as offset boundary clues, not a complete layout: AI field block this+0x32C8..0x461C, shared vehicle fields this+0x34E0..0x34F8, pit/command-queue fields this+0x413C..0x461C, and obj-base fields obj+0xCD4/0xD14/0xD18/0xD58/0x32C8/0x4040/0x4064/0x4068/0x4094/0x48A4/0x48A8. The this vs obj bases are kept distinct per the no-merge rule; the obj-base samples may belong to a distinct unnamed sub-object (see conflicts and unresolved).

canonical_type_families.name: WaypointNode
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Waypoint-graph node reached through the vehicle pointer fields (this+0x4354 current, 0x4358 chain base, 0x4364 third chain node, 0x4400 lead reference, forward-link at +0x114). Holds position, tangent, up-vector, track distance, lateral boundaries, grip/traction, heading and node-id/pit-entry flag.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 19 GUESS field samples across bases *(this+0x4354), *(this+0x4358), *(this+0x4364), *(this+0x4400) and *(*(this+0x4400)+0x114); same-offset reads on different chain bases are kept as boundary clues, not merged into a single layout. No method ownership in the packet.

canonical_type_families.name: RacingLineSteeringController
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame AI steering-target computation: 5-lane boundary scan, centre-steering computation, lane scoring via spatial nearest-neighbour queries, and overtaking state transitions on the vehicle.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No field samples in the packet; class defined by single method 0x004270A0 with a DERIVED legacy-ABI lead. Lane/steering state lives in the F1CVehicle AI field block; no separate struct layout claimed.

canonical_type_families.name: AIDifficultyCurve
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Interpolates the AI difficulty slider onto an ability value using three anchor constants (flt_5EA3DC / flt_5EA3E0 / flt_5EA3E4); slider > 100 interpolates mid-to-high, otherwise low-to-mid.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No field samples; single-method interpolation class. The anchor constants are globals, listed under unresolved_evidence_refs for the exact scaling meaning.

canonical_type_families.name: PitStrategy
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Fuel and stint sufficiency decisions for AI pit timing: compares remaining laps (reduced by a stint factor) against a fuel-consumption estimate, with an early-TRUE path when the FuelMult check is disabled.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No field samples; per-vehicle fuel fields (this+0x403C/0x4040/0x3984/0x3448) are covered by the F1CVehicle family; this class contributes only the decision method.

canonical_type_families.name: AI_Push_Lap_Closing_Gap
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame qualifying push-lap strategy for the player vehicle: target-lap adjustment, performance scalar and tire-compound recommendation with pit-exit forcing on mismatch or low average tire wear.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No field samples; single-method player-vehicle strategy. Its per-vehicle fields (tire-wear slots, target-lap and performance fields) are covered by the F1CVehicle family.

canonical_type_families.name: Pit_Part_State_Copy
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Destination pit-stop part-state struct whose fields are filled by copying part data, tire brand/compound, and scoring intervals from a source vehicle state, then returning the pit-stop state transition.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 22 GUESS/DERIVED field samples at this+0xC..0x18C (callback lists, part data/flags, tire brand/compound, scoring interval slots, callback counts); treated as boundary clues for a distinct pit-stop part-state struct, not merged into F1CVehicle.

canonical_type_families.name: TirePhysicsModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-vehicle tire physics model built from HDV data and applied per wheel: per-wheel compound application, slip-curve resolution, and suspension-ratio output.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 6 GUESS/DERIVED field samples at this+0x60/0x64/0x68/0xAC/0x145C/0x1F00 (step constants, suspension-ratio output, compound index, physics context handle). Possible identity with F1CVehicleTireSystem is left open (no overlapping offsets in the packet); see conflicts.

canonical_type_families.name: F1CPitMachine
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Owns the pit-stop lifecycle: mode dispatch from event records, pit-box alignment checks, readiness evaluation, per-frame progress/servicing and pit-exit sequencing (speed limiter, wheel-force ramps, state-4 notify).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 19 DERIVED/GUESS field samples at this+0x0..0x1D4 (vehicle pointer, mode/mode-value, readiness flag, entry/completion/elapsed timing, mid flag, limiter base/timestamp/ceiling/engaged, wheel-force window base/end); ownership marked abi:reviewed by the packet. Kept distinct from F1CVehicle: the vehicle is reached only through the VehiclePtr at this+0x0.

canonical_type_families.name: F1CVehicleTireSystem
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Large float-table-bearing tire physics object: grip coefficient, force solvers (bisection, friction-circle), lateral force, force/torque model, engine wear slots, scrub reset and audio pitch scaling. Class grouping is DERIVED from strong field overlap (0x3A70/0x3514/0x3C40/0x3D64/0x32BC) plus the constructor that owns them.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 53 DERIVED/GUESS field samples across a torque/force constant block (this+0x1EC..0x2E8) and a float-table block (this+0x32BC..0x3D70: rigid-body constraint, lateral-slip scale, force tables, bracket table, drag, wear slots +0x3D64..0x3D70). Field samples are boundary clues; table strides and the 918-element special stride in ScaleAudioPitch are unresolved.

canonical_type_families.name: F1CAIRacingLineTracker
canonical_type_families.responsibility: AI racing-line path following and per-frame path-position tracking: node chain traversal, target node resolution, orientation/position state, suspension and wheel-contact updates, rigid-body constraint solving.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 17 DERIVED field samples at this+0x3440..0x3A9C (path mode, rotation matrix this+0x34B0..0x34D0, target position this+0x34D4..0x34DC, orientation this+0x34E0..0x34E8, constraint-solve counter this+0x3A9C). Vehicle fields it reads (obj+0x4040 target node id, obj+0x4094 step flag) are covered by the F1CVehicle family.

canonical_type_families.name: WheelSuspensionGeometry
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-wheel suspension/tire state initialization against the chassis local origin: wheel offset from chassis origin, suspension parameters, rotation matrix and Euler extraction. Owner is UNKNOWN in the packet; separated from F1CVehicleTireSystem because its wheel-state layout (74-float stride) and origin fields are distinct.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 3 DERIVED chassis-origin field samples at this+0x48/0x4C/0x50; the wider wheel-state layout written by the function has no packet field evidence and stays unresolved.

canonical_type_families.name: AIOpponentSelector
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Builds the performance-ranked, deduplicated AI opponent roster for path assignment using a float-key merge sort. Owner UNKNOWN; class and list-field layout DERIVED from the single function's output-list writes.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 4 DERIVED/GUESS output-list field samples at this+0x0 (head) / 0x4 (tail) / 0x8 (secondary) / 0xC (count); roster node layout and the merge-sort key remain unresolved.

canonical_type_families.name: TireBrandTable
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Tire brand name catalog with 36-byte-stride entries and gated not-found debug reporting.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 2 DERIVED field samples: entry count at this+0x0 and table pointer at this+0x4; entries are 36-byte stride with brand-name pointer at entry offset 0.

state_machines.name: DriverStatusMachine
transitions: pit-wait timer 0x4170 < now -> driverStatus = 4 (session type 0x7C56A4==7) else 5, then re-arm pit-exit timer 0x447C
0/6 -> SteeringAngleController (0x00425670); 6 -> 7 when |heading error| < 0.5 or 0x447C elapsed
0x447C snapshot timer -> toggle 6/0 and snapshot position into 0x4470/0x4474/0x4478
1 -> sub_4258C0; 2 -> FieldZeroSetter and return; 3 -> waypoint squared-distance vs 0x461C -> 0 when farther, else update 0x461C
steering-error accumulator 0x446C > 0x4558 -> driverStatus = 1 (after RaceStartCountdownStateUpdate when gear 0x39FC > 2)
7 -> zero 0x442C/0x4438/0x4434; Speed 0x4440 < 0.2 -> driverStatus = 0
racing-line reset path -> driverStatus = 4/5 by 0x7C56A4; pit-return 5 -> 3 after tier selection or -> 0

state_machines.name: PitStopDecisionMachine
transitions: PitStopBlockingCondition or session != 7 -> not service-ready; when session==7 set RetiredFlag 0x4410=1, clear AIControlFlag 0x45F4, log via sub_4BC060
service-ready path -> tire-compound tier selection and SpeedValueSetterWithGlobalMirror + PostPitCleanup

state_machines.name: AIPitStateMachine
transitions: Idle -> PitRequested: AI command id 1 schedules the pit decision timer (this+0x413C = session time + 2.0)
PitRequested -> PitLaneActive: AI command id 4 enables the pit state via sub_4A46F0(this, 1, 1)
PitLaneActive -> Idle: AI command id 5 clears this+0x4548 and disables the pit state via sub_4A46F0(this, 0, 0)
Idle -> PitRequested: pit-window phase (dword_7C56A8 == 5) with a sub-1 fuel multiplier forces a pit exit (ForcePitExit)
Any -> Blocked: last-lap, teammate-part, or finish-state guard blocks ForcePitExit
Any -> Blocked: race phase dword_7C56A8 == 8 blocks pit requests (PitStopBlockingCondition)

state_machines.name: AICommandQueue
transitions: Idle -> Pending: append an 8-byte {command, value} entry at +0x44A8 and store the new index at +0x44B0
Pending -> Pending: re-send the queued response when the command is already present (dedup scan)
Pending -> Idle: after CommandQueueResponseHandler (0x00429EE0), the index at +0x44B0 resets to -1
Pending -> Full: append denied when index + 1 reaches capacity +0x44AC; the index is restored to its previous value

state_machines.name: PitMachineState
transitions: Event mode byte at a2+8 differs from this+0x184 -> store it and call AIPitStrategyState on the base vehicle
Vehicle sub-state obj+0x32C8 == 2 or 3 -> dispatch on mode this+0x184 (2 -> sub_4A5EA0, 0 -> sub_4A5F20)
PitMid flag fires in the last 2.0s before completion (this+0x1A4)
StateChangeNotify(state 4) leaves the pit stop
AI reason code obj+0x4068 == 9 cleared to 0 when the limiter deactivates

state_machines.name: EngineWearMode
transitions: Four wear slots +0x3D64..0x3D70 initialized to FLT_MAX before any mode check
Wear recompute runs per frame when dword_7CEA5C in (0, 2]
Wear value divided by flt_8ACF9C when dword_7C56A4 == 7 and dword_7CEA5C == 2
TireScrubReset clamps wear slot +0x3D64 (or global dbl_7C91DC) gated by dword_7CEA5C

interfaces.name: SpatialWaypointQuery
interfaces.purpose: Nearest-neighbour, plane-test and indexed-field copy queries over the shared waypoint spatial tree (dword_5EA2C0) used by racing-line, waypoint-following and steering.

interfaces.name: AICommandQueue
interfaces.purpose: AI command-message queue: dispatch of pit-lane/waypoint-set commands (message id 14) and ring-buffer input selection for the AI tick.

interfaces.name: PitEntryRequest
interfaces.purpose: Request an AI pit entry by setting the call-to-box flag or forcing pit state, gated by race-session, fuel, and wear conditions.

interfaces.name: DifficultyScaling
interfaces.purpose: Map the AI difficulty slider global onto an AI ability scalar, either as a flat capped value or an anchored interpolation.

interfaces.name: DriverEventReporting
interfaces.purpose: Emit driver-table events (retirement, failure, pit) into the session event table anchored at flt_5EA618 via InsertDriverTableEntry.

interfaces.name: TireCompoundPhysics
interfaces.purpose: Initialize and apply the per-vehicle/per-wheel tire compound physics model from HDV data.

interfaces.name: PitMachineDelegateDispatch
interfaces.purpose: Conditional dispatch into optional pit-machine sub-objects (crew, delegates) guarded by pointer fields this+0x8/+0xC/+0x10 and vehicle-control state.

interfaces.name: TireForceTableQuery
interfaces.purpose: Sign-selected force-table interpolation with friction-circle clamping shared by the tire force solvers.

interfaces.name: TireBrandCatalogQuery
interfaces.purpose: Name-based tire brand lookup over a fixed-stride table.

interfaces.name: OpponentRosterQuery
interfaces.purpose: Performance-ranked opponent list construction with name deduplication and float-key merge sort.

compatibility_contracts.name: ControlOutputCommitContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Every AI tick path must write committed control outputs into the input fields this+0x3580 (throttle), this+0x3584 (brake), this+0x357C (steering) before returning; the racing fallthrough writes neutral (0, 1.0, 0). A replacement executable must preserve this commit location and neutrality.

compatibility_contracts.name: DriverStatusContract
compatibility_contracts.description: driverStatus at this+0x4510 must keep the documented 0..7 semantics: pit entry forces 4 or 5 (session type 0x7C56A4==7 selects 4), 6 is follow-target steering, 7 stops the car until Speed<0.2, and the racing-line reset forces 4/5 by the same session-type rule.

compatibility_contracts.name: AIEnableGateContract
compatibility_contracts.description: aiEnableFlag at this+0x32C8 gates the whole AI tick: AIMainUpdate returns immediately when >1, and the racing tick re-checks obj+0x32C8==1. A replacement must preserve both guards.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitLaneFlagContract
compatibility_contracts.description: PitLaneRouteFlag this+0x4548 and the pit-lane byte this+0x45F4 steer the pit-box/pit-lane steering overrides in computeSteeringTarget and gate the pre-race init path in AIMainUpdate; PitStopDecisionTireCompound sets 0x4548=1 on entry.

compatibility_contracts.name: WaypointTreeContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The waypoint spatial tree dword_5EA2C0 and its count/global neighbours (0x5EA2CC, 0x5EA2D0) back the nearest-neighbour queries; waypoint node id at +0x12C and the set selector this+0x4550 drive pit-lane command dispatch (message id 14).

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionPhaseContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Global session type dword_7C56A4 and phase dword_7C56A8 select the driver-status pit values, the countdown/launch ramp (dword_5C30E0 / dword_5C3144 tables, global byte_5C3160), the ability drift, and the retirement path; simulation time dbl_8AFEA0 is the shared clock for all timers.

compatibility_contracts.name: RetiredFlagContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Retirement sets RetiredFlag at this+0x4410 and clears AIControlFlag at this+0x45F4, then logs through sub_4BC060; AIDriverStructInit clears both when a session (re)starts.

compatibility_contracts.name: CallToBoxValueGate
compatibility_contracts.description: SetCallToBox writes only 0 or 1 to vehicle+0x454C; any input value greater than 1 is ignored and the field keeps its prior value. A replacement must preserve this gate.

compatibility_contracts.name: AIPitDecisionTimer
compatibility_contracts.description: AI command id 1 writes vehicle+0x413C to session time (dbl_8AFEA0) + 2.0, scheduling the pit decision timer.

compatibility_contracts.name: DriverEventTypeCodes
compatibility_contracts.description: InsertDriverTableEntry on the session table at flt_5EA618 consumes driver-table type codes 41, 1, 2, 42, 52, 272 and 273, with the magic sentinel -2.0 used for unfilled time arguments.

compatibility_contracts.name: AICommandQueueLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The AI command queue stores 8-byte {command, value} entries in the buffer at +0x44A8 with capacity at +0x44AC and index at +0x44B0; already-pending commands are deduplicated by re-sending the queued response, and a full queue restores the prior index instead of overwriting.

compatibility_contracts.name: MainTick400
compatibility_contracts.description: The main game tick converts session time (dbl_8AFEA0 * 400) to a tick count; the tick counter dword_7C5698 wraps at 400 and dword_7C5694 is clamped so the pending tick delta never exceeds 201.

compatibility_contracts.name: TractionModeShift
compatibility_contracts.description: The tire model step is derived as 400 >> dword_7CE958 and its traction constants are published to the globals dbl_5E5238 and dbl_5E5240; consumers outside this packet depend on those globals.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitStopScoringIntervals
compatibility_contracts.description: CopyPitPartState fills three scoring interval slots at this+0x164/0x16C/0x174 with fixed starts (1024/2048/3072) when the scoring scale is zero, or with CRTFtol cumulative distances offset by dword_7D0374 otherwise.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitMachineStateDispatchContract
compatibility_contracts.description: A replacement must preserve mode-byte dispatch at this+0x184, vehicle sub-state gating at obj+0x32C8 (values 2/3), optional-delegate ordering via this+0x8/+0xC/+0x10, event-value storage at this+0x188, and StateChangeNotify(state 4) on pit exit.

compatibility_contracts.name: PitStopTimingContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Pit stop timing and limiter-ramp fields must persist: entry this+0x1A0, completion this+0x1A4, elapsed this+0x1A8, mid flag this+0x1AC, limiter base/timestamp/ceiling this+0x1B0..0x1B8, engaged this+0x1C0, wheel-force windows this+0x1C4/0x1D0/0x1D4; limiter deactivation must write the ceiling and clear AI reason code 9 (obj+0x4068).

compatibility_contracts.name: TireForceTableLayoutContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Sign-selected force tables (+0x3C40 positive scaled by +0x3C3C, +0x3C80 negative scaled by +0x3C7C), aero tables (+0x3C00 scaled by +0x3BFC, +0x3CC0 scaled by +0x3CBC), contact-patch array +0x39D0 with count +0x39F8 and lerp table +0x39A4, mode selector +0x39B4, and friction-circle slip fields +0x3A70/+0x3514/+0x3518 with a [0,1] clamp.

compatibility_contracts.name: TireWearModeContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Four wear slots at +0x3D64..0x3D70 clamp to FLT_MAX; per-frame recompute gated by dword_7CEA5C in (0,2], noise seed dword_8AAE70, optional division by flt_8ACF9C when dword_7C56A4==7 and mode==2; TireScrubReset clamps slot +0x3D64 when the +0x32BC field is nonzero.

compatibility_contracts.name: AudioPitchScaleContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Per-frame pitch ratio a2 / this+0x3BF4; flag-gated array scaling via byte_7D01C4 bits 0-2 (sub_5881F0 paths, pitch field +0x3984, 8-byte-strided +0x39A4 array, +0x39D0 array scaled by the reciprocal ratio), ending with the TireBrushModelForceSolver call.

compatibility_contracts.name: OpponentRosterLayoutContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Output list fields head/tail/secondary/count at this+0x0/+0x4/+0x8/+0xC; float-pair nodes (8-byte allocation via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper) merge-sorted by float key; roster size read at vehicle-setup +0x14; name dedup with the byte_5EA438 empty fallback.

compatibility_contracts.name: TireBrandTableLayoutContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Brand table at this[1] (this+0x4) with a 36-byte stride; entry offset 0 is the brand-name pointer; count at this+0x0; miss path logs a non-existent-tire message gated by dword_7C569C != 5.

conflicts.subject: 0x0042A110 name semantics (ForcePitExit vs RequestPitEntry)
alternatives: RequestPitEntry (packet ABI lead; disassembly enters pit state 1 and sets CallToBox=1)
conflicts.resolution: Not resolvable from packet evidence alone; kept as a single F1CVehicle function whose role is pit-entry request/forcing, flagged for later cross-check against callers 0x00429470 and 0x0042A180.

conflicts.subject: Field this+0x4550 dual semantics
conflicts.resolution: Not reconciled: both reads are evidenced on the same field by different functions; the per-function names are preserved and the ambiguity recorded for live verification.

conflicts.subject: Field this+0x45E0 triple use
alternatives: tire-change counter incremented when the change flag is clear (0x0042A6F0)
conflicts.resolution: Three functions read/write the same offset with different roles and no unification evidence in the packet; recorded as an unresolved multi-use field.

conflicts.subject: Field this+0x45F4 naming conflict
alternatives: AIControlFlag cleared on retirement (RetiredFlagContract) / aiControlFlag (wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_01 F1CVehicle)
conflicts.resolution: Same offset, two contracts from the same source proposal disagree on the role; both describe write/clear semantics; kept as a conflict pending live verification, no merge forced.

conflicts.subject: Field obj+0x32C8 / this+0x32C8 naming
alternatives: aiEnableFlag / objAiEnable gating the whole AI tick (vehicle_ai_and_pit_01)
conflicts.resolution: The AI-tick gate (==1) and the pit-machine sub-state dispatch (==2/3) may be the same field read under different phase conditions; not reconcilable from packet evidence and both names are preserved.

conflicts.subject: dword_7C56A8 == 8 race-phase meaning
alternatives: race phase blocks pit requests (existing-analysis prose)
conflicts.resolution: The packet evidences only the literal comparison; the phase meaning is DERIVED from existing analysis and must not be promoted to CONFIRMED on this evidence.

conflicts.subject: dword_7CEA5C engine wear mode semantics
conflicts.resolution: Raw source wins over the existing-analysis mode set; exact mode semantics remain unverified and the field stays named by offset.

conflicts.subject: TirePhysicsModel vs F1CVehicleTireSystem identity
conflicts.resolution: Both are tire-physics objects with no overlapping field offsets in the packet; kept as separate families per the no-merge rule, with the possible identity left open for live verification.

conflicts.subject: F1CVehicle merged from three proposals
alternatives: single F1CVehicle family spanning AI-tick, pit/command-queue and vehicle-root methods
three separate families (one per source proposal)
conflicts.resolution: Merged into one canonical family because all three proposals name the same class, the responsibilities agree (per-vehicle state container), and call relationships connect the method sets; the wave_001_vehicle_ai_and_pit_02:6 obj-base samples are kept as boundary clues and a distinct unnamed sub-object may exist (see unresolved).

unresolved: Owner identity for 0x00425670, 0x00429470, 0x0042B0E0, 0x00409F40 and 0x0040B360 is UNKNOWN in the packet; they are not assigned to a class and only reach the F1CVehicle AI field block through their confirmed callers.
Dual role of this+0x454C (CallToBox command input in computeSteeringTarget vs waypoint node-id key for chain-link resolution in AIRacingLine/AIWaypointSteeringUpdate) is not resolved.
Vtable dispatch targets behind 0x00409F40 (slot +0x18 then +0x1C) and 0x0040B360 (slots +24/+28) are unresolved; concrete callees are unknown.
Speed-profile array length (20) and the tire-record scan base (0x4600, up to 7 entries) are literals not present in packet field metadata.
Indexed array write at this + 4*(this+0x4148) + 0x3D70 lands inside the car-conditions buffer; element meaning unresolved.
Lane-table (0x4174) 68-byte entry layout and the candidate ownership of the obj+0x48A4/0x48A8 overtake-allowance counters are inferred from pointer arithmetic, not a named struct.

Dozens of read-only float/double tuning constants in 0x59E43C..0x59E99C and unk_7CE2F0 / dword_7CEC30 / dword_8ACEE0 are read by the functions but have no visible use in the decompiled bodies; presumed consumed inside inlined callees.
AI command-queue message id 14 and the semantics of sub_4A46F0 are not established from packet evidence.
Stride-slot targets of the reinit loops (anchors +0x41B4, +0x42D8, +0x4144) beyond the packet-listed anchors are not named.
Waypoint-graph link navigation is by array index in the raw; the node layout beyond the packet-listed offsets stays unresolved.
Field pairs this+0x4560/0x4564/0x4568 (countdown light timers) and this+0x442C/0x4438 (brake/throttle output pair) keep offset-based names; the packet provided no semantic names.

Name conflict for 0x0042A110: the historical name 'ForcePitExit' conflicts with the packet ABI lead 'RequestPitEntry' (disassembly enters pit state 1 and sets CallToBox=1). Not resolvable from packet evidence alone.
